question: Under W.S. 33-28-109(a), what is the maximum number of real estate companies or sole proprietorships a resident Responsible Broker may lawfully establish within Wyoming?
choice_a: One
choice_b: Two
choice_c: Three
choice_d: There is no statutory limit
explanation: W.S. 33-28-109(a) permits a resident Responsible Broker to lawfully establish at least one but no more than three real estate companies or sole proprietorships in Wyoming, acquiring a license for each. Choice D is wrong because the statute expressly caps the number at three.

question: WREC Rules Chapter 1 requires that, before a Real Estate Company License is issued, the Responsible Broker hold which relationship to the company?
choice_a: Only a W-2 employee with no equity interest
choice_b: A minority shareholder only, with no management role
choice_c: No formal relationship to the company is required
choice_d: Officer, partner, or manager, or hold an ownership interest in the company
explanation: Chapter 1, Section 6(b) of the WREC rules requires the Responsible Broker to be an officer, partner, or manager of, or hold an ownership interest in, the real estate company. A mere employee with no equity or managerial role (A) does not satisfy this requirement.

question: Before WREC will issue a Real Estate Company License to a Responsible Broker, what must first be verified?
choice_a: That the Secretary of State of Wyoming shows the company is in good standing
choice_b: That the company has passed a state real estate examination
choice_c: That the company owns real property located in Wyoming
choice_d: That the company has operated for at least five years
explanation: Chapter 1, Section 6(a) provides that a Real Estate Company License is issued to the Responsible Broker upon verification by the Wyoming Secretary of State that the company is in good standing. There is no five-year operating history requirement (D).

question: A resident Responsible Broker who operates as a sole proprietorship under W.S. 33-28-109(a) is subject to which rule?
choice_a: Must obtain a separate real estate company license in addition to the individual license
choice_b: Is not required to acquire an additional company license
choice_c: May not maintain a fixed office
choice_d: Must register the sole proprietorship as a branch office
explanation: W.S. 33-28-109(a) specifically exempts a resident Responsible Broker operating as a sole proprietorship from having to acquire an additional real estate company license, unlike a broker organizing a separate company entity.

question: Under W.S. 33-28-122(a)(i), a Responsible Broker's trust or escrow account must be structured so that it:
choice_a: Earns a fixed rate of interest payable to the broker
choice_b: Requires a 30-day hold before any withdrawal can be made
choice_c: Permits immediate withdrawal of the funds deposited in it
choice_d: Is held at an out-of-state depository for added security
explanation: W.S. 33-28-122(a)(i) requires the trust or escrow account to permit immediate withdrawal of deposited funds; in lieu of maintaining such an account, the broker may instead use a funds holder. The account must be at an in-state financial institution, not out-of-state (D).

question: WREC Chapter 5 requires that money belonging to others (cash or check) be deposited into the listing Responsible Broker's trust account or with a funds holder no later than:
choice_a: The same calendar day it is received
choice_b: Three business days after receipt
choice_c: Ten calendar days after receipt
choice_d: The first banking day after receipt, unless all persons with an interest in the funds have agreed otherwise in writing
explanation: WREC Chapter 5, Section 1(e)(v) requires deposit no later than the first banking day after receipt by the listing Responsible Broker, per W.S. 33-28-122(a)(i), unless all interested parties have agreed otherwise in writing. There is no same-day, three-day, or ten-day standard.

question: Under W.S. 33-28-122(e), a Responsible Broker's deposit of his own funds into a trust account is NOT considered commingling if:
choice_a: The deposit is made only to open the account or avoid a minimum-balance charge, and is identified at the time of deposit
choice_b: The broker's personal funds exceed 50% of the account balance
choice_c: The broker withdraws the funds again within 24 hours
choice_d: The funds are never separately itemized
explanation: W.S. 33-28-122(e) carves out a narrow exception: depositing personal funds solely to open the trust account or avoid a minimum-balance charge is not commingling, provided that deposit is identified at the time it is made. Failing to itemize (D) would actually undermine this exception, not satisfy it.

question: If a Wyoming trust account is interest-bearing and there is no written agreement among the interested parties regarding the interest, W.S. 33-28-122(c) requires that when funds are withdrawn and paid out, the accrued interest:
choice_a: Is retained by the Responsible Broker as additional compensation
choice_b: Is paid out proportionally to the person(s) receiving the underlying funds
choice_c: Is forfeited to the State of Wyoming
choice_d: Is donated automatically to the WREC recovery fund
explanation: Absent a written agreement, W.S. 33-28-122(c) requires interest to be paid out to the person(s) from whom the trust funds were received, in the same proportion as the funds withdrawn bear to the total deposit. The broker has no right to keep the interest as compensation (A).

question: When there is a dispute over the return or forfeiture of earnest money held in trust, W.S. 33-28-122(f) requires the Responsible Broker to continue holding the funds until:
choice_a: Thirty days pass, automatically releasing the funds to the seller
choice_b: The buyer's attorney authorizes release
choice_c: He obtains a written release from the parties, a civil action is filed, or he interpleads the parties
choice_d: The Commission's next scheduled audit occurs
explanation: W.S. 33-28-122(f) requires the broker to continue holding disputed deposit funds in trust until he has a written release from the parties consenting to disposition, a civil action is filed, or he interpleads all parties, at which point the funds may be paid to the court. There is no automatic 30-day release rule (B).

question: In a cooperative transaction where the buyer's broker receives cash or a check as earnest money, W.S. 33-28-122(g) requires that, absent a different agreement of the parties:
choice_a: The buyer's broker deposits it directly into his own trust account
choice_b: The funds are split evenly between both brokers' trust accounts
choice_c: A title company automatically takes possession of the funds
choice_d: The buyer's broker delivers the contract and the cash or check to the seller's broker, who deposits it in his trust account
explanation: W.S. 33-28-122(g) requires that, unless otherwise agreed, the buyer's broker deliver the contract and the cash or check to the broker working with the seller, who then deposits it in his own trust account. If a promissory note or thing of value is received instead, the seller's broker holds it rather than depositing it.

question: WREC Chapter 5 requires a Responsible Broker to reconcile trust/escrow account journals and ledger liabilities monthly by proving agreement among which three figures?
choice_a: The journal cash balance, the sum of the cash balances for all ledgers, and the corresponding bank account balance
choice_b: Listing price, sale price, and commission earned
choice_c: Buyer's deposit, seller's net proceeds, and the broker's fee
choice_d: Prior year balance, current balance, and projected year-end balance
explanation: Chapter 5, Section 1(e)(vii)(C) requires the monthly bank reconciliation worksheet to prove agreement between the cash balance in the account journal, the sum of the cash balances for all ledgers, and the corresponding bank account balance, listing each beneficiary's ledger balance as of the reconciliation date.

question: When a Responsible Broker collects money in advance for services or advertising expenses that have not yet been performed, WREC Chapter 5 provides that no money may be withdrawn from those funds (except for actual expenses paid on the principal's behalf) until:
choice_a: Thirty days have elapsed since collection
choice_b: The Responsible Broker has fully performed the services for which the principal contracted
choice_c: The listing agreement expires
choice_d: The Commission grants written approval
explanation: Chapter 5, Section 1(k) requires advance fees for services or advertising to be deposited with a funds holder or in trust, and bars withdrawal (other than actual expenses paid on the principal's behalf) until the broker has fully performed the contracted services. There is no fixed 30-day or Commission pre-approval requirement.

question: After withdrawing advance-fee funds from a principal's trust account under WREC Chapter 5, within how many days must the Responsible Broker furnish the principal a full, itemized accounting?
choice_a: Ten (10) days
choice_b: Sixty (60) days
choice_c: Twenty (20) days
choice_d: No deadline is specified by rule
explanation: Chapter 5, Section 1(k) requires a full and itemized accounting to be furnished to the principal within twenty (20) days of any withdrawal of the principal's advance-fee funds from the trust or funds holder account.

question: WREC Chapter 5 requires that, unless otherwise permitted, money belonging to others be deposited according to the purpose of the transaction, keeping sales escrow deposits in a separate account from:
choice_a: The broker's advertising budget
choice_b: The Commission's audit fund
choice_c: The real estate company's payroll account
choice_d: Property management deposits and security deposits
explanation: Chapter 5, Section 1(e) requires separate types of escrow accounts by purpose — for example, sales escrow deposits kept separate from property management deposits, which are in turn kept separate from security deposits.

question: Under W.S. 33-28-102, a Wyoming "funds holder" is statutorily defined as:
choice_a: A title company, closing agent, or attorney licensed in Wyoming who holds items of value in trust for the parties to a real estate transaction
choice_b: Any bank that offers escrow account services
choice_c: Any licensed real estate salesperson designated by the broker to hold funds
choice_d: The Wyoming Real Estate Commission itself
explanation: W.S. 33-28-102(b)(xxi) defines a "funds holder" as a title company, closing agent, or attorney licensed in Wyoming who holds items of value in trust for the parties to a real estate transaction — a distinct, alternative mechanism to a broker's own trust account, not simply any bank (A).

question: When a Responsible Broker elects to deposit trust monies with a funds holder rather than maintaining his own trust account, W.S. 33-28-122(a)(ii) requires the broker to:
choice_a: Keep the arrangement confidential from the transaction parties
choice_b: Disclose his intent to use a funds holder and its name to all parties to the contract, and notify the Commission in writing
choice_c: Obtain a real estate license for the funds holder
choice_d: Deposit a matching amount in his own personal account
explanation: W.S. 33-28-122(a)(ii) requires the broker to disclose his intention to use a funds holder and the funds holder's name to all parties to any contract, purchase agreement, lease, or lease agreement, and to identify all funds holders used and notify the Commission in writing — the opposite of keeping it confidential (A).

question: WREC Rules Chapter 1 requires an applicant for a Responsible Broker License to submit proof of which of the following as part of the application?
choice_a: A funds holder agreement only — proof of a personal trust account is never accepted
choice_b: A personal line of credit sufficient to cover client funds
choice_c: Wyoming trust account(s) or funds holder agreement(s)
choice_d: A surety bond posted in lieu of any trust accounting
explanation: Chapter 1, Section 3(c)(iii) requires a Responsible Broker License applicant to provide proof of Wyoming trust account(s) or funds holder agreement(s) — either satisfies the requirement, contrary to choice B's claim that only a funds holder agreement is acceptable.

question: A nonresident Responsible Broker licensed in Wyoming who engages in real estate activity in the state must, per WREC Chapter 5, maintain trust accounts:
choice_a: In his home state only
choice_b: Anywhere in the United States of his choosing
choice_c: Only through an account administered directly by the Wyoming Real Estate Commission
choice_d: With a Wyoming funds holder, or in a bank or recognized depository located in Wyoming
explanation: Chapter 5, Section 1(h) requires a nonresident Responsible Broker engaged in Wyoming real estate activity to maintain separate trust accounts with a Wyoming funds holder or in a bank or recognized depository located in Wyoming, not in his home state (A).

question: When trust funds are transferred to a funds holder, WREC Chapter 5 requires the Responsible Broker to:
choice_a: Obtain a receipt showing the date and the amount of the funds transferred to the funds holder
choice_b: Destroy his own copy of the transaction file
choice_c: Notify only the buyer of the transfer, not the seller
choice_d: Wait sixty days before confirming the transfer occurred
explanation: Chapter 5, Section 1(e)(vi) requires that when trust funds are held by a funds holder, the Responsible Broker obtain a receipt showing the date and amount of funds transferred, as the starting point for his own recordkeeping.

question: Under W.S. 33-28-109(a), if a Responsible Broker moves the address of his designated office, he must:
choice_a: Notify the Commission within 90 days after the move has occurred
choice_b: Apply to the Commission before the removal, designating the new location, and pay the required fee
choice_c: Simply update his business cards and signage
choice_d: Take no action as long as the company's trade name is unchanged
explanation: W.S. 33-28-109(a) requires the Responsible Broker to apply to the Commission before removal from a designated address, designating the new location and paying the required fee, whereupon the Commission issues a license for the new location. Notice after the fact (A) does not satisfy this requirement.

question: W.S. 33-28-102 defines an "office," for purposes of the real estate licensing act, as:
choice_a: Any location where a licensee happens to meet with clients
choice_b: The Wyoming Real Estate Commission's headquarters in Cheyenne
choice_c: A Responsible Broker's place of business where records are maintained
choice_d: A branch location that does not require a separate license
explanation: W.S. 33-28-102(b)(xxxvi) defines "office" as a Responsible Broker's place of business where records are maintained — a fixed, licensed location, not simply any meeting spot (B).

question: Under WREC Rules Chapter 1, an applicant establishing a home-based real estate company must, among other submissions:
choice_a: Obtain a separate certified appraiser permit
choice_b: Pay double the standard company licensing fee
choice_c: House the business in a structure detached from the residence
choice_d: Attest that establishment of the business complies with applicable county and/or city zoning and codes
explanation: Chapter 1, Section 6(c)(v) requires an applicant establishing a home-based business to attest that the business is established in accordance with county and/or city zoning and codes.

question: Under W.S. 33-28-123, a Responsible Broker must retain a full set of records for every real estate transaction in which he participates for not less than:
choice_a: Two (2) years from the latest date on which the real estate company participated in the transaction
choice_b: One year from the closing date
choice_c: Five years from the date of the listing agreement
choice_d: Indefinitely, with no minimum retention floor set by statute
explanation: W.S. 33-28-123 requires a Responsible Broker to keep and maintain a full set of transaction records for not less than two years from the latest date on which the real estate company participated in the transaction — a defined statutory floor, contrary to choice D.

question: For each funds holder account maintained, WREC Chapter 5 requires the Responsible Broker to keep a recordkeeping system that includes, at minimum:
choice_a: Only the buyer's name and the final sale price
choice_b: Date received/paid, check number, amount, buyer, seller, escrow agent, date delivered, description of the real estate, and disposition of the transaction
choice_c: A copy of the buyer's personal credit report
choice_d: The listing agent's continuing education transcript
explanation: Chapter 5, Section 1(e)(vi) enumerates the minimum fields required for the funds-holder recordkeeping system: date received/paid, check number, amount, buyer, seller, escrow agent, date delivered, description of the real estate, and disposition of the transaction.

question: For every real estate company and/or branch location, WREC Chapter 5 requires a Responsible Broker to maintain both a journal showing the chronological sequence of funds received and disbursed with a running balance, and:
choice_a: A separate payroll ledger for each affiliated licensee
choice_b: A monthly marketing expense report
choice_c: A transaction ledger showing the receipts and disbursements as they affect each particular buyer/seller or landlord/tenant transaction
choice_d: An annual property appraisal log
explanation: Chapter 5, Section 1(e)(vii)(A)-(B) requires both a chronological journal with a running balance and a transaction ledger reflecting receipts and disbursements for each specific transaction between the parties.

question: Under W.S. 33-28-109(b), a licensed branch office of a Wyoming real estate company must:
choice_a: Operate under a trade name entirely separate from the principal office
choice_b: Have its own independent Responsible Broker unrelated to the main office
choice_c: Be located in a different county than the principal office
choice_d: Use the same trade name or business name as the licensed real estate company
explanation: W.S. 33-28-109(b) requires a branch office to use the same trade name or business name as the licensed real estate company; every branch office remains under the direction and supervision of the Responsible Broker, not an unrelated broker (C).

question: When a Responsible Broker applies for a branch office license, W.S. 33-28-109(b) requires the broker to also submit:
choice_a: A plan of supervision for the branch office, for approval by the Commission
choice_b: A five-year business plan for the branch
choice_c: A separate errors and omissions insurance policy for each branch
choice_d: Proof that the branch office will generate a minimum annual revenue
explanation: W.S. 33-28-109(b) requires that, in addition to the branch office application, the Responsible Broker submit a plan of supervision for the branch office for Commission approval — there is no minimum revenue or five-year plan requirement.

question: Under WREC Chapter 6 (Regulatory Enforcement Grounds), which of the following is expressly listed as unprofessional conduct by a Responsible Broker?
choice_a: Taking a scheduled vacation during an active listing period
choice_b: Failing to supervise the activities of his associate broker or salesperson
choice_c: Charging a commission below the local market average
choice_d: Referring a client to a broker licensed in another state
explanation: Chapter 6 lists, among grounds for disciplinary action, a Responsible Broker's failure to supervise the activities of his associate broker or salesperson. Ordinary business choices such as pricing (B) or referrals (C) are not disciplinary grounds.

question: WREC Chapter 6 permits a Responsible Broker to pay earned real estate compensation to a corporation or LLC solely owned by a licensee working under him. This arrangement:
choice_a: Transfers the legal duty to supervise that licensee to the corporation or LLC
choice_b: Automatically converts the licensee into an independent contractor exempt from supervision
choice_c: Does not relieve the Responsible Broker of the obligation to supervise the licensee or any other requirement of the act or Commission rules
choice_d: Requires the licensee to surrender his individual real estate license
explanation: Chapter 6, Section 3(e) makes clear that paying compensation to a licensee's wholly-owned corporation or LLC does not violate the prohibition on compensating unlicensed persons, but any such agreement does not relieve the Responsible Broker's duty to supervise the licensee.

question: If a Responsible Broker manages two or more real estate companies and is representing a buyer or seller in a transaction involving those companies, W.S. 33-28-302(j) requires the broker to:
choice_a: Choose only one of the companies to represent in the transaction
choice_b: Refer the transaction to a competing brokerage
choice_c: Dissolve one of the companies before proceeding with the transaction
choice_d: Immediately appoint a transaction manager for each real estate company involved, unless the other licensee is an associate broker
explanation: W.S. 33-28-302(j) requires that where a Responsible Broker is representing a buyer or seller in a transaction involving two or more companies he manages, he must immediately appoint a transaction manager for each real estate company, unless the other licensee involved is an associate broker.

question: W.S. 33-28-302(j) requires a Responsible Broker who supervises more than one real estate company to:
choice_a: Disclose in every real estate transaction to all parties involved the names of all real estate companies the Responsible Broker supervises
choice_b: Keep the existence of the other companies confidential from transaction parties
choice_c: Disclose the other companies only upon a party's written request
choice_d: Disclose the other companies only to the Commission, never to transaction parties
explanation: W.S. 33-28-302(j) affirmatively requires the Responsible Broker to disclose, in every real estate transaction, the names of all real estate companies he supervises to all parties involved — not merely on request (B) or to the Commission alone (D).

question: If a Responsible Broker's branch office maintains a separate trust account, W.S. 33-28-122(b) requires that office to:
choice_a: Share a single combined bookkeeping system with the principal office
choice_b: Maintain a separate bookkeeping system
choice_c: Forward all trust funds daily to the principal office instead of keeping records
choice_d: Close the separate account within 90 days of opening it
explanation: W.S. 33-28-122(b) requires that if a branch office maintains its own separate trust account, that office must maintain a separate bookkeeping system, rather than commingling records with the principal office (A).
